maya: Quick heads-up — PM moved the holiday promo window to a 72hr distributed burst starting Dec 2 UTC. They want <1s P95 for chat and >=80k embed ops/hr for search. Can infra ops sketch capacity needs?

sam: Ack. Need a few numbers: expected peak concurrent requests, average tokens per request, and acceptable queuing latency.

maya: PM says peak QPS ~2.5k chat requests, avg 60 tokens output, 1.2 reqs/sec per session. Search embed bursts: 80k ops/hr concentrated in three 30-min spikes.

linh: Quick calc — assuming a 25ms/token GPU throughput for our quantized 13B on p4x2ish, 60 tokens = 1.5s per req. With 2.5k QPS that's 3750 token-s threads/sec -> wait that's messy. I'll run a small sim and post numbers.

raj: We should consider warm pools. Cold-start KV cache wipes add ~200ms per warmup on long context models. If we prewarm prefix caches across nodes it's ~30% lower latency overall.

sam: If we treat chat and embed tiers separately: chat needs low latency instances (dedicated low p99), embed can be batched aggressively on cheaper gpus or burst to spot. Tradeoff is regional capacity and preemption risk.

kevin: Cost quick-lookup: reserved p4-* costs ~$$ per GPU-hr (see billing spike runbook). Spot options drop 60% but preempt time could ruin SLA. For a 72hr promo I'd lean hybrid: reserved baseline + spot for spike.

linh: Simulation output (very rough):
```
inputs: {qps:2500, tok_per_req:60}
model: 13B-quant
throughput_per_gpu_tok_s: 500
=> needed_gpus_chat = ceil((2500*60)/500) = ceil(300000/500) = 600 gpus
batching: continuous batching might reduce tokens/s pressure by ~1.7x => effective gpus ~350
```
This is coarse but shows order of magnitude.

sam: 350 GPUs dedicated for chat peak is big. Can we reduce by using a smaller latency-optimized model or compiler-level kernel perf? Also KV caching and prefix caching could cut effective load.

maya: Product is reluctant to reduce quality for the promo. They prefer routing lower-value traffic to a smaller model instead.

raj: Suggestion: route experimental or unverified traffic to a cheaper 6B quant, keep 13B for sessions with +conversion signals. Also set per-customer rate limits to avoid a few customers burning all capacity.

scheduler-bot: [autoscaler] dry-run: prewarm_plan created for region us-west-2: 120 reserved gpus, 230 spot candidates, prewarm_start=2025-12-01T20:00:00Z

kevin: Ops math: if we commit 120 reserved + assume 200 spot sustained for spike windows, and effective batching saves 1.7x, we might hit ~ (120+200)*500 tok_s = 160k tok_s which supports ~2666 reqs of 60 tokens => borderline. Need cross-region overflow.

linh: Cross-region overflow to eu-west helps but network egress and added latency might push p95 above SLA. Need SLO-aware routing: route lower-latency sessions to us-west until queue > X then overflow non-interactive workloads.

sam: Also think about autoscale cooldowns and controller limits — rapid 3x QPS jumps in 5 minutes can cause thrash. We should predefine a surge policy: allow immediate burst by maintaining a small warm buffer equal to ~20% of predicted peak.

maya: Action items: 1) eng-infra: run a high-fidelity sim with real kernel perf numbers by EOD today. 2) devex: build routing rule to send low-value sessions to 6B for promo window. 3) product/security: confirm allowable cross-region fallback. 4) finance: approve spot+reserved spend for 72hr window.

raj: I'll draft a playbook snippet for eviction and graceful fallback (how to swap to 6B mid-session vs start-of-session).

kevin: Finance — rough cost estimate for hybrid 72hr: reserved baseline 120 GPUs x72hr + avg spot 200 GPUs x36hr (only during peaks) = estimate ~X00k. Need approval.

maya: If infra gives numbers by EOD we can decide conservative reserve and toggle spots. Please ping if you need sample traces.

sam: I'll run the sim now with a 10k-sample trace (will post results in thread).

kevin: FYI — tagging finance @finance for budget ok.

scheduler-bot: [incident] prewarm job scheduled: id=hp-2025-12-01-1, eta=2025-12-01T20:00:00Z

maya: Thanks everyone — we need a short runbook for the on-call shift covering 72hr window. Draft incoming. :pray:
